# Sirach Chapter 34 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_034_page_001.jpg

---

**34:1** Empty hopes and false illusions belong to the senseless, and dreams give wings to fools.

**34:2** Like one who grasps at a shadow or chases the wind is anyone who gives heed to dreams.

**34:3** What is seen in a dream is nothing but a reflection, the image of a face looking at a face.

**34:4** From an unclean thing, what can be made clean? And from something false, what can be true?

**34:5** Divinations and omens and dreams are empty, and the heart fantasizes like a woman in childbirth.

**34:6** Unless they are sent as a visitation from the Most High, give them no attention.

**34:7** For dreams have led many astray, and those who set their hope in them have come to ruin.

**34:8** The law will be fulfilled without falsehood, and wisdom is made complete in the mouth of the trustworthy.

**34:9** A person who has traveled widely has acquired much knowledge, and one with broad experience can speak with understanding.

**34:10** One who is inexperienced knows little, but a well-traveled person gains great discernment.

**34:11** In my travels I have seen many things, and I understand more than I can put into words.

**34:12** Many times I have been in mortal danger, but I have been rescued through these very experiences.

**34:13** The spirit of those who fear the Lord will live, for their hope is in the one who saves them.

**34:14** Whoever fears the Lord will not be afraid and will not play the coward, for the Lord is his hope.

**34:15** Blessed is the soul of the one who fears the Lord! On whom does he rely, and who is his support?

**34:16** The eyes of the Lord watch over those who love him — a powerful protection and a strong support, a shelter from the hot wind and a shade from the noonday sun, a guard against stumbling and a defense against falling.

**34:17** He lifts the spirit and makes the eyes shine; he gives healing, life, and blessing.

**34:18** If someone brings a sacrifice from wrongfully obtained goods, the offering is defective, and the gifts of the lawless are unacceptable.

**34:19** The Most High takes no pleasure in the offerings of the ungodly, nor is he appeased for sins by a multitude of sacrifices.

**34:20** Like killing a son before his father's eyes is the person who brings a sacrifice from the property of the poor.

**34:21** The bread of the needy is their life; whoever withholds it is a killer.

**34:22** Depriving a neighbor of his livelihood is murder, and defrauding a hired laborer of his wages is bloodshed.

**34:23** When one person builds and another tears down, what have they gained except hard work?

**34:24** When one prays and another curses, whose voice will the Lord hear?

**34:25** If someone washes after touching a corpse and then touches it again, what good was the washing?

**34:26** So it is with the person who fasts for his sins and then goes out and does the same thing again: who will hear his prayer, and what has he gained by his self-humiliation?
